cards.text: Right before this, Zion said, 'The LORD has forsaken me; the Lord has forgotten me!' (Isa 49:14). Now the LORD speaks, and He opens with a question: 'Where is your mother’s certificate of divorce with which I sent her away?'
Then question number two: 'Or to which of My creditors did I sell you?' Friend, I got sold for a quarter out of a clearance bin, so trust me, I know what being sold feels like.

cards.question: The LORD tells His people the real reason they were sold and their mother was sent away. What is it?

answers.text: Debts the LORD owed to others

cards.text: Next He asks, 'Why was no one there when I arrived? Why did no one answer when I called?' Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer hoping somebody would call my name, and here the LORD is calling and NOBODY picks up.

cards.question: The LORD asks if His hand is too short to redeem His people. True or false: He says He lacks the strength to deliver them.
Instead, the LORD shows His power. He says He turns rivers into a desert. What does His rebuke do to the sea?

cards.text: And the fish rot for lack of water and die of thirst. Friend, when the FISH are thirsty, you know you're dealing with Somebody.

cards.question: The LORD says He clothes the heavens in ___ and makes sackcloth their covering.

cards.text: Now a new voice speaks: the LORD's Servant (Isa 50:10). The Servant says, 'The Lord GOD has given Me the tongue of discipleship, to sustain the weary with a word.'

cards.question: A disciple is a learner. Morning by morning, what does the Lord GOD do for the Servant?

answers.text: Sends Him a dream at night
Shows Him a vision of heaven

cards.text: Morning by morning, friend. The Servant wakes up ready to listen every single day, and I can't get through ONE morning without hitting snooze three times.

cards.question: The Lord GOD has opened the Servant's ears. True or false: the Servant says He turned back.

cards.text: Then it gets hard. The Servant says, 'I offered My back to those who struck Me, and My cheeks to those who tore out My beard.'

cards.question: True or false: when people scorn the Servant and spit on Him, He hides His face.
Because the Lord GOD helps Him, the Servant says He has set His face like ___.

cards.text: A face like flint, friend. Mine? One baker frowns at my butterscotch bits and my whole face folds like warm dough.

cards.question: Then the Servant asks, 'Who will dare to contend with Me?' Why is He so bold?

answers.text: The One who vindicates Him is near
His enemies have all run away
An army stands right behind Him

cards.text: Then He says, 'Who has a case against Me? Let him approach Me!' Meanwhile, somebody leaves ONE bad review about my sprinkles and I'm hiding behind the oven for a WEEK.

cards.question: The Lord GOD helps the Servant, so who can condemn Him? He says they will all wear out like a ___, and the moths will devour them.

cards.text: Then a question goes out to everyone listening: 'Who among you fears the LORD and obeys the voice of His Servant? Who among you walks in darkness and has no light?'

cards.question: Someone fears the LORD but walks in darkness and has no light. What is that person told to do?

answers.text: Trust in the name of the LORD

cards.text: Walking in the dark with no light? I lived there, friend. Years in the back of a junk drawer, and the only thing I had to lean on was an old takeout menu.
But then comes a warning: 'Behold, all you who kindle a fire, who array yourselves with firebrands, walk in the light of your fire and of the firebrands you have lit!'

cards.question: Some walk by the light of fires they lit themselves. They're told, 'This is what you will receive from My hand.' What is it?

findings.problem: No story card sets up Isaiah 50:3. The card just before it is about the fish. The blank asks the baker to guess the exact wording (black, gold or light). Nothing told so far lets them reason it out, and 'light' is just as believable as 'black' for the heavens.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The question spends card words defining a hard word: 'A disciple is a learner.' Hard words get a dictionary pop-up.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The card only restates what card 2 just answered (morning by morning, the Servant's ear is awakened to listen) and adds a snooze joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. The joke should ride on a card that tells new text.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card only recaps card 7's answer ('A face like flint') and adds a joke. It tells no new text. The rest of Isaiah 50:7 ('I have not been disgraced... I know that I will not be put to shame') is never told, and this card could carry it. The joke also nearly repeats card 10's joke: a critic of his toppings makes him crumble.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card only recaps Isaiah 50:10 ('Walking in the dark with no light?'), which card 12 already told. It adds a drawer joke but no new part of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: 'The only thing I had to lean on was an old takeout menu' contradicts the backstory. In the drawer he had friends who were all in it together, and he welcomed every newcomer. The line also adds a new drawer detail.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The question merges the two questions in Isaiah 50:10 into one person ('Someone fears the LORD but walks in darkness'). The text asks them as two separate questions and doesn't say how they connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 15 introduces Isaiah 50:11 as 'a warning'. That setup rules out the wrong answers 'A place of rest' and 'A place of honor', so only 'A place of torment' fits.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: All three true or false cards (stop 1 card 5, stop 2 cards 4 and 6) have False as the right answer, and each one is built the same way: a statement that the opposite of the verse happened. A baker could learn to tap False without reading.
findings.question: Should the true or false cards in a walkthrough mix True and False right answers? Does the 'No formula' rule cover the pattern of right answers, or only question types and order?
